records.detail: Session 2026-09-26/27 (commit a5178d6, local only, not pushed). Development clustering job 64633773 completed (106,729,566 comparisons; clusters sha 60296a43, comparisons sha 670d8147) and resume verification job 64793946 reproduced the recorded hashes. Development chaining is mild, contrary to the earlier prediction: the largest single-linkage cluster holds 739 of 10,334 isolates (7.2 percent), versus 1,314 of 3,159 in the external set. Duplicate-pair job 64925356 completed with verified artifact.sha256: 41,016 putative-duplicate development pairs at the frozen 99.99 ANI / 0.95 AF rule, involving 4,347 isolates (pairs sha 4ea3a285); Rule G cannot be applied until MLST lineages exist. Blocker 13 resolved: scripts/normalize_jarbs_ast.py normalizes the frozen JARBS table to 7,605 MIC-eligible isolate-drug rows from 2,535 isolates with structural counts only (external set remains sealed), and construct_research_cohort.py accepts repeated --interpreted-ast with per-source hashes in the manifest. A genome-provenance contract (registered assembly versus raw reads assembled here, source accession, genome SHA-256) is enforced from metadata through validation. Genomics redesigned to run on the 13,493 checksum-verified disjointness assemblies via hpc/unity/genomics-setup.sbatch, genome-analysis-array.sbatch and scripts/finalize_genome_analyses.py (species by skani ANI>=95 and AF>=50 percent against type strain GCF_003697165.2). Setup job 64925569 froze AMRFinderPlus database 2026-08-07.1 from probe 64689133 (162 files hashed) but failed on three defects now fixed with regression tests: quast 5.3.0 needs distutils so the QC env pins python 3.11, mlst ran under system perl so tools now run with their env first on PATH, and the species check compared the display name so it now requires NCBI taxonomy species taxid 562 plus type-material label (reference is the neotype, strain taxid 866789). Resubmitted as 64925955. Verification: 274 local tests pass, tiny end-to-end workflow 8/8, 121 tracked files synced to Unity with identical SHA-256, Unity test job 64925755 exit 0. No phenotype model was fitted and no claim is added.

Genomics setup job 64925955 completed exit 0 after the fixes: QUAST v5.3.0, mlst 2.35.0 (mlst --check OK), AMRFinderPlus 4.2.7 with frozen database 2026-08-07.1, skani 0.3.1; species reference GCF_003697165.2 verified as NCBI taxonomy species 562 and neotype material, reference.fna sha256 17124ac56df45b547706ddb0b2a56274d893022f42fe445afb5a08e19eb874b1. Canary array 64926291 on six genomes (two registered development assemblies, two development raw-read assemblies, two external raw-read assemblies) completed in 3m16s with every tool exit 0 and peak RSS 0.5 GB; scripts/finalize_genome_analyses.py (job 64926910) marked all six species-confirmed (ANI 98.2-98.5 percent, query AF 83-88 percent against the type strain), QC PASS, MLST PERFECT with lineage assigned, and eligible for modelling. Array resources were reduced to 4 GB and 1 hour from the canary measurement, and the full array 64927454 (1,350 tasks of 10 genomes, at most 60 concurrent, cpu partition) was submitted over all 13,493 verified assemblies. MLST adequacy criteria were drafted in amendment 004 before any cohort-level MLST output exists and await the decision owner; the cohort-level ST distribution will not be read until they are adopted. No phenotype was read.

Decision owner adopted the amendment 004 MLST adequacy criteria on 2026-09-27, before any cohort-level MLST output was read (full array 64927454 was running and only per-genome completion counts had been viewed). Criteria are frozen in config/study.json splitting.lineage_adequacy (typing coverage >= 0.95 else escalate to cgMLST; largest ST <= 0.40 and inverse Simpson >= 10 else reopen amendment 004) and implemented in scripts/assess_lineage_adequacy.py over eligible development genomes per population (human_clinical and all_sources), worst outcome wins, non-zero exit unless keep_st, no phenotype or external genome read. Boundary arithmetic is exact (integer half-coverage and n^2/sum n_i^2), after a test caught a floating-point off-by-one. Verification: 285 local tests pass, tiny end-to-end workflow 8/8.

Post-genomics chain made end-to-end testable and queued. A new end-to-end test (tests/test_pipeline_integration.py: finalize, lineage adequacy, isolate metadata from split development and external cluster files, cohort from NCBI plus JARBS-normalizer MICs, validation) caught a defect that would have silently excluded every raw-read genome: construct_research_cohort.py required a non-blank assembly_accession, but the 3,159 external genomes and 348 development genomes are assembled here from reads and have none. Blank is now allowed only for genome_source raw_reads, mirroring the validator. On the real data all 348 raw-read development isolates have blank AST assembly accessions, all 9,986 registered isolates match their requests exactly, and BioSamples agree for all 10,334. The validator now reports external censoring fractions as sealed because they approximate resistance prevalence; the fully-censored structural check still runs. build_isolate_metadata.py accepts repeated --clusters and refuses double assignment. hpc/unity/cohort-build.sbatch verifies all source checksums and that every requested genome is COMPLETE, then runs finalize, lineage adequacy (stops unless ST kept), metadata, construction and validation, writing COMPLETE only on validation pass; submitted as 64927962 with afterany dependency on array 64927454. Unity input hashes match local: NCBI normalized AST 653c89a7 (recorded), source attributes 21ffd670, JARBS normalized e6decd01. 296 local tests pass; 125 tracked files synced identically.

Genome-analysis array 64927454 completed all 1,350 tasks: 13,493 of 13,493 genomes COMPLETE, zero batch failures. Finalize inside cohort build 64927962: external 3,159 genomes, 3,157 species-confirmed, 3,104 QC pass and eligible; genome exclusions across both cohorts 90 contig count, 3 length, 22 N50, 5 species not confirmed; development 10,295 of 10,334 eligible. The build then stopped at lineage adequacy with escalate_cgmlst (typing coverage 0.592 all sources, 0.716 human clinical; concentration and diversity checks passed). That outcome is VOID: the array ran mlst --scheme ecoli, which in mlst 2.35.0 is the Pasteur scheme (dinB icdA pabB polB putP trpA trpB uidA), not the Achtman scheme amendment 004 specifies (ecoli_achtman_4: adk fumC gyrB icd mdh purA recA). Evidence: the installed scheme files and every mlst.tsv name scheme ecoli with Pasteur alleles; the top ST was Pasteur ST43, the Pasteur counterpart of Achtman ST131. The finalizer's scheme check expected the pre-2.23 name and the canary checked only typing success. Criteria unchanged. Remediation (commit on main, local only): config/study.json genomics.mlst freezes the scheme and loci; finalize_genome_analyses.py fails closed on any other scheme or loci and reads a checksum-verified re-typing tree via --mlst-root; hpc/unity/mlst-array.sbatch re-types all verified assemblies into results/genomics/mlst/ecoli_achtman_4 leaving Pasteur outputs untouched; cohort-build.sbatch requires complete re-typing. Void run recorded in docs/GROUPING_VARIABLE_AMENDMENT.md. 302 local tests pass, tiny workflow 8/8, 126 tracked files synced identically. MLST canary 64939197 submitted.

Achtman MLST canary 64939197: six genomes typed with scheme ecoli_achtman_4 and loci adk fumC gyrB icd mdh purA recA, all checksums verified; the ST131 isolates carry the canonical ST131 profile (adk53 fumC40 gyrB47 icd13 mdh36 purA28 recA29). Full re-typing: array 64939241 on cpu ran one task at a time under low fair-share priority (FairShare 0.40), so its pending tasks 2-269 were moved to cpu-preempt as array 64939277 (x86_64 constraint; tasks of about four minutes, resumable via COMPLETE markers, within the Unity preempt guidance for jobs under two hours), and cohort build 64939242 now depends on both arrays. Blocker 11 in progress: scripts/evaluate_mic_predictions.py implements interval-censored scoring (reference dilution sets per comparator, essential and exact agreement over all rows and exact-only, two-step over and under calls, bias, Gaussian interval log-likelihood, whole-lineage bootstrap, external rows refused unless --locked-external) with 13 tests; docs/MIC_EVALUATION_SPEC.md is PROPOSED and awaits the decision owner. Development dilution-scale audit (development only): 25,466 MIC rows, 23 distinct values, all mg/L, 18,136 censored; all but 3 rows (0.2, 2.5, 200 mg/L) lie within 0.1 log2 of a doubling dilution. Latent defect fixed: build_split_manifest.py balanced folds on ast_category, absent under mic_regression, and reported external rows by category; it now balances development rows on censoring class within population and reports external rows by antibiotic count only. 318 local tests pass, tiny workflow 8/8, 129 tracked files synced identically.

Achtman re-typing completed (arrays 64939241 and 64939277) and cohort build 64939242 passed lineage adequacy (keep_st: typing coverage 0.99 in both populations; largest ST131 10.7 percent of all sources and 23.8 percent of human clinical, above one fold share and reported; inverse Simpson 43.4 and 12.4). It then failed closed at amendment 005 rule G: 929 of 19,771 development putative-duplicate pairs cross STs, above the prespecified 1 percent trigger, so amendment 004 is reopened. Diagnosis on development genotypes only: of cross-ST pairs with both isolates typed, 970 of 1,007 differ at exactly one MLST locus and 37 at two, none at more (for example ST131 with its single-locus variant ST9126, which has no clonal complex assigned). Candidate groupings measured: ST 1,222 groups, largest 10.7 percent; single-locus-variant-linked STs 492 groups, largest 11.0 percent (the ST131 complex of 16 STs), human-clinical inverse Simpson 10.9; ST joined by duplicate pairs 1,159 groups, largest 10.8 percent. Proposed revision (awaiting decision owner) recorded in docs/GROUPING_VARIABLE_AMENDMENT.md: lineage_group becomes the single-locus-variant group. No phenotype was read.

Decision owner adopted on 2026-09-27 (a) the amendment 004 revision: lineage_group is the single-locus-variant group over eligible development Achtman STs, named SLV:ST<n>, with other genomes joining their ST group or a unique SLV-adjacent development group and never merging development groups (finalize_genome_analyses.assign_slv_groups, 5 tests); and (b) docs/MIC_EVALUATION_SPEC.md: essential agreement over all rows as primary with exact-only reported beside it, credit only relative to the no-genome baseline, and exclusion of values more than 0.1 log2 off the doubling scale (construct_research_cohort.py, reason mic_value_off_doubling_scale; 3 tests including tolerance parity with the evaluator). Both were adopted before any model was fitted or external MIC read. scripts/run_mic_baseline.py implements the prespecified no-genome comparator (intercept-only interval-censored normal per antibiotic, fitted on training folds, both populations); a test recovers mu -1.0 and sd 1.5 from simulated censored data. hpc/unity/development-baseline.sbatch builds lineage-grouped folds, runs the baseline and evaluates it on development only. Cohort build resubmitted as 64939994 with development-baseline 64940008 queued afterok. 332 local tests pass, tiny workflow 8/8, 132 tracked files synced identically.

Cohort build 64939994 ran every stage end to end for the first time: lineage adequacy keep_st under SLV groups, isolate metadata with rules I and G passing, and cohort construction from NCBI plus JARBS MICs yielding 24,732 development and 4,464 external isolate-antibiotic MIC rows (external: counts only). Validation failed on two validator defects, not data defects: (1) 11,014 'invalid' collection dates were valid INSDC year-only (10,172) and year-month (839) dates plus 3 blanks, rejected because pandas inferred the full-date format from the first row; dates are now validated as YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD with a calendar check and never completed; (2) 59 absent countries ('not collected' 35, empty 24) and 3 absent dates, which amendment 006 keeps absent, are now MIC-profile warnings (kept for lineage-grouped evaluation, excluded from geographic and forward-time holdouts); categorical still requires them. Note added to docs/COUNTRY_AND_POPULATION_AMENDMENT.md. 334 local tests pass, tiny workflow 8/8, Unity synced identically. Cohort rebuild 64940231 and development baseline 64940232 (afterok) submitted; stale baseline 64940008 cancelled.

First validated MIC research cohort: build 64940231 COMPLETE, validation PASS, artifact checksums verified; research_cohort.csv sha256 76d6f48ed355b0ffa06e9ff9778881d8bfc2679fbde140b2163bf13003d9aa7d; 29,196 isolate-antibiotic rows from 11,377 isolates. Development 9,889 isolates (human clinical 3,843): ceftriaxone 2,819 human clinical / 6,974 all sources, ciprofloxacin 3,806 / 8,370, gentamicin 3,342 / 9,388. External (counts only) 1,488 isolates with all three drugs, 4,464 rows. Isolate metadata: 13,493 requested; development 10,068 and external 1,816 retained; exclusions: external by frozen membership 1,270, genome not eligible 39 development and 55 external, lineage unresolved 101 development, specimen source absent 126 development and 18 external; 490 development SLV lineage groups; rule G passed. Cohort exclusions: 3 off-scale MIC values, 269 non-MIC rows. Warnings: 59 country and 3 date absent in source; site and surveillance network absent. Development baseline job 64940232 COMPLETE (checksums verified): 5 lineage-grouped folds of 4,600 to 5,751 rows over 486 CV groups; isolate_splits.csv sha256 c48e6f79. The prespecified no-genome baseline (intercept-only interval-censored normal) fits degenerately because development MICs are bimodal and heavily censored at both panel limits: ceftriaxone human clinical fitted mean 2^-24 to 2^-15 mg/L with sd 29 to 30 log2, exact-reference rows only 156 of 2,819. Its all-row essential agreement (human clinical: ceftriaxone 0.721, ciprofloxacin 0.539, gentamicin 0.732; all sources 0.774, 0.700, 0.816) comes largely from agreeing with left-censored rows by predicting absurdly low values, while exact-only EA is 0.000 to 0.135 except all-sources gentamicin 0.920. Development data only; no genomic model fitted; no external MIC read.

Rebuilt MIC cohort after the decision owner's specimen-source and baseline decisions: build 64948707 COMPLETE, validation PASS, checksums verified; research_cohort.csv sha256 6b066cfdab16871287a51331e8942e69f071a06b4971d1746ee0d53ad921ed0d; 29,619 rows from 11,520 isolates. Development 10,015 isolates (human clinical 3,849): ceftriaxone 2,822 human clinical of 7,097, ciprofloxacin 3,809 of 8,493, gentamicin 3,348 of 9,514; 492 SLV lineage groups. External (counts only) 1,505 isolates with all three drugs. 143 isolates without specimen source are now kept blank; most also lack country and date and are population undetermined, so absent-in-source warnings rose to country 332, date 333, specimen 423 rows while human clinical gained 6 isolates. Remaining metadata exclusions: genome not eligible 39 development and 55 external, lineage unresolved 101 development and 1 external, external by frozen membership 1,270. Development baseline 64948708 COMPLETE (checksums verified), isolate_splits.csv sha256 ca272d23. Best-constant no-genome baseline, lineage-bootstrap 95 percent intervals, human clinical: ceftriaxone predicts 0.0625 mg/L, EA 0.721 [0.583, 0.866], exact-only 0.000 of 157 exact; ciprofloxacin 0.016 mg/L, EA 0.599 [0.408, 0.826], exact-only 0.481; gentamicin 1-2 mg/L, EA 0.823 [0.733, 0.923], exact-only 0.791. All sources: ceftriaxone 0.767, ciprofloxacin 0.747, gentamicin 0.811. The wide intervals reflect whole-lineage resampling. Development data only; no genomic model fitted; no external MIC read.

Holdout and precision analysis on validated cohort 64948707 (development comparators and genotype only; no external MIC or comparator read; no model fitted). Uniting SLV lineage groups, 99.9 percent ANI genomic clusters and deduplication groups gives 485 development units versus 489 lineage groups, so genomic clusters (2,711, largest 717) nest inside lineages. Human clinical has 218 lineage groups, inverse Simpson 10.9, SLV:ST131 24.4 percent. External-locked cohort: 1,505 isolates in 106 lineage groups, 18 in groups absent from development. Conservative precision planning (ICC of the above-panel indicator within lineage, DEFF = 1 + (m_w - 1) ICC, planning EA 0.90): human clinical half-widths ceftriaxone 0.090 (ICC 0.276, n_eff 43), ciprofloxacin 0.126 (ICC 0.496, n_eff 22), gentamicin 0.065 (ICC 0.135, n_eff 82); all sources 0.056, 0.081, 0.042; external at an assumed ICC of 0.10: 0.072 (n_eff 66). Amendment 007 (docs/EVALUATION_DESIGN_AMENDMENT.md) PROPOSED: nested lineage-grouped cross-validation replaces the internal holdout; the CV unit absorbs genomic clusters (4 merges); precision planned from the development error ICC of the first genomic model before unsealing, target half-width 0.05.

Decision owner adopted amendment 007 on 2026-09-27 with two additions (docs/EVALUATION_DESIGN_AMENDMENT.md): nested lineage-grouped cross-validation replaces the internal holdout; the CV unit unites SLV lineage group, 99.9 percent ANI genomic cluster and deduplication group, with a guard that stops the split only if clusters chain units beyond the largest lineage or duplicate unit and one fold's share; external precision is planned from the development error ICC of the first genomic model before unsealing, target half-width 0.05; a tuning-free nearest-relative baseline (highest-ANI other-fold relative in the same population, predicting its reference-set boundary) joins the no-genome baseline; and every result is also reported for SLV:ST131 and for all other lineages (config evaluation.dominant_lineage). Implemented: build_split_manifest.py, evaluate_mic_predictions.py stratification, build_amr_features.py (AMRFinderPlus Type AMR elements, complete or contig-end calls, per-report hash check), run_neighbor_baseline.py (single stream of the 9 GB comparison table, ordered pairs counted once), run_censored_regression.py (ridge-penalised interval-censored normal regression with analytic gradient; nested CV with in-fold feature filtering at five training isolates and inner grouped folds choosing the penalty on inner essential agreement). Tests verify the gradient against finite differences, recovery of known effects (+3, +2, 0 log2) from censored data, and that test-fold-only features never enter a fold's model. 359 local tests pass, tiny workflow 8/8, 140 tracked files synced identically. Development modelling job 64960056 submitted on cohort 64948707.

First development modelling round (job 64960056, 12m41s, checksums verified; cohort 64948707; 485 CV units). AMR features: 13,399 genomes, 129,155 AMR calls, 1,137 distinct elements (acquired 95,216; point 31,174; point-disrupt 2,765). Nearest relatives across lineage-grouped folds have median ANI 99.12 (human clinical) and 99.25 (all sources). Known-mechanism censored regression, nested CV, human clinical EA with lineage-bootstrap 95 percent CI: ceftriaxone 0.920 [0.894, 0.948], ciprofloxacin 0.913 [0.891, 0.939], gentamicin 0.885 [0.866, 0.910]; SLV:ST131 0.874, 0.888, 0.851; other lineages 0.933, 0.921, 0.896. Largest coefficients are the expected mechanisms (CTX-M-15/27/14/55 and CMY-2 for ceftriaxone; qnrS1, gyrA S83L and D87N, qnrB19 for ciprofloxacin; aac(3)-IId/IIe and rmtB1 for gentamicin). Paired comparison (job 64961738, identical rows, paired whole-lineage bootstrap), human clinical, model minus no-genome constant: ceftriaxone +0.199 [+0.080, +0.312], ciprofloxacin +0.314 [+0.092, +0.498], gentamicin +0.062 [-0.027, +0.138] (not distinguishable); minus nearest relative: +0.227, +0.347, +0.072 [-0.012, +0.146]. All sources: every difference positive with intervals excluding zero (ceftriaxone +0.158, ciprofloxacin +0.170, gentamicin +0.113 versus constant). The nearest-relative baseline scored below the no-genome constant in every drug and population: across lineage-grouped folds relatedness does not transfer. Weaknesses: exact-reference EA is low (human clinical ceftriaxone 0.248, gentamicin 0.343 versus constant 0.791), and the penalty selected most often was the smallest in the grid (0.1), so the grid must extend downward. Amendment 007 precision planning, fixed now from this first genomic model before unsealing: development error ICC 0.010 to 0.048 (versus 0.14 to 0.50 for the phenotype itself); external half-widths at planning EA 0.90: human clinical ceftriaxone 0.052 (underpowered, just above the 0.05 target), ciprofloxacin 0.048, gentamicin 0.033; all sources 0.037, 0.046, 0.027 (adequate). Development only; no external MIC value or comparator read.

Round 2 development modelling (job 64965891, 9m37s, checksums verified; same folds, features and baselines as round 1 job 64960056; modelling environment job 64965836: xgboost 2.1.4, scikit-learn 1.8.0, scipy 1.17.1, numpy 2.4.2, pandas 2.3.3; local tests used xgboost 3.4.1). Widened ridge grid: selections now interior (at most 1 of 5 folds at an edge) and EA unchanged versus round 1 (differences -0.002 to +0.001). XGBoost AFT, human clinical: ceftriaxone EA 0.929 [0.900, 0.957], ciprofloxacin 0.918 [0.900, 0.940], gentamicin 0.894 [0.861, 0.931]; paired gain over round-1 ridge +0.009 [-0.003, +0.018], +0.006 [-0.001, +0.012], +0.009 [-0.009, +0.029], none distinguishable; gentamicin still not distinguishable from the no-genome constant (+0.071 [-0.007, +0.133]). All sources: 0.942, 0.933, 0.932, gains over ridge +0.017 [+0.010, +0.024], +0.016 [+0.010, +0.024], +0.008 [+0.003, +0.012]. XGBoost raised exact-reference EA (human clinical ceftriaxone 0.210 to 0.490, gentamicin 0.343 to 0.441) but its interval log-likelihood is worse in human clinical (ceftriaxone -0.590 versus -0.393) because the AFT scale is fixed at 1.0 and not tuned. In all sources the deepest trees (depth 4) were selected at the grid edge in 4 of 5 ceftriaxone and 3 of 5 ciprofloxacin folds. Foundation-model protocol revision 0.2 (targeted resistance loci instead of whole genomes; measured Evo 2 20B rate about 7,300 bases per second on H100, whole genomes about 5,000 GPU-hours versus about 60 for loci) is PROPOSED and awaits the decision owner. Development only; no external MIC read.

Foundation-model protocol revision 0.2 adopted by the decision owner on 2026-09-27 (docs/FOUNDATION_MODEL_PROTOCOL.md): Evo 2 embeds resistance-relevant units instead of whole genomes. Rationale measured on Unity: prior Evo 2 20B jobs 56562342/56562343 on H100 embedded 0.42 Mb in 130 s and 1.41 Mb in 266 s (about 7,300 bases per second after a ~70 s load), so whole assemblies on both strands (~138 Gb) would need about 5,000 GPU-hours, and a whole-genome mean would mostly encode lineage. Units: 12 K-12 MG1655 chromosomal loci with 300 bp upstream (gyrA, gyrB, parC, parE, marR, acrR, soxR, ampC, ompF, ompC, ompR, envZ), located by blastn at >= 80 percent identity over >= 90 percent of the unit, else missing; and every complete AMRFinderPlus acquired gene with 500 bp flanks. Panel reference GCF_000005845.2 built by job 64966441 (unit lengths 735 to 2,928 bp; gyrA 2,928 = 2,628 + 300). Extraction array 64966442 (67 tasks) and collection 64966443 submitted on cohort 64948707. scripts/embed_resistance_units.py embeds deduplicated units on both strands with candidate layers blocks.6/12/17 mlp.l3 in one pass, averages strands, records reverse-complement cosine, and writes hash-checked resumable shards; hpc/unity/embeddings-units.sbatch runs on gpu-preempt H200 NVL (the only partition with H200) in under-2-hour resumable tasks, reading the existing Evo 2 weights offline. Canary 64966506 (20 sequences) queued after collection. No phenotype read.

Resistance-unit extraction complete (array 64966442, 67 tasks; collection 64966443; checksums verified): 13,399 genomes, 287,069 unit rows deduplicated to 31,938 unique sequences (56.3 Mb), about 4 to 7 GPU-hours for Evo 2 20B on both strands instead of the 60 estimated. Panel loci found in 94 to 99.9 percent of genomes (gyrA, gyrB, parC, parE, envZ, ompR, soxR at least 99.7 percent; ompF lowest at 93.7 percent, 610 truncated at contig ends); unfound loci recorded missing, never imputed; 126,281 acquired units. The H200 NVL node (gpu-preempt only) was estimated to start the canary on 2026-09-29, so on the decision owner's approval the run moved to H100 80GB on the non-preemptible gpu partition (x86_64, the hardware of the prior Evo 2 20B runs). First H100 canary 64980720 failed in 4 s ('module: command not found' in a batch shell); fixed by sourcing Lmod, with a test requiring every job that calls module to load Lmod first. Canary 64983712 passed on uri-gpu009 (NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3; evo2 0.5.5, torch 2.7.1; flash-attn 2.8.3 above the transformer_engine-declared range, recorded): 20 units, 66,548 bases on both strands in 14.8 s including warm-up (4,483 bases per second), peak GPU memory 43.15 GB, all 8,192-dimensional vectors finite, shard checksum verified; reverse-complement cosine median 0.966 (blocks.6), 0.899 (blocks.12), 0.983 (blocks.17, minimum 0.560). Production array 64983760 (4 tasks, H100) submitted; Evo 2 model round 64983779 (ridge and XGBoost AFT on amr, amr+evo2 and evo2 feature sets, per-locus PCA refitted in every training set, layer chosen on inner folds) queued afterok. No phenotype read by any embedding step.

Pre-registration, decision owner 2026-09-28 (commit a34bfca, 14:44 UTC), before any all-sources Evo 2 result or external MIC was read: (1) Evo 2 credit rule in docs/FOUNDATION_MODEL_PROTOCOL.md: credited per antibiotic only if AMR+Evo 2 beats AMR alone for both learners in human-clinical development nested CV with paired lineage-bootstrap intervals excluding zero, and on the locked external evaluation, with the overlap audit reported; all-sources results cannot create credit. At adoption only gentamicin met the development condition (ridge +0.027 [+0.010, +0.038]; XGBoost +0.024 [+0.001, +0.043]). (2) MIC_EVALUATION_SPEC addendum A: every model reported by reference class with the right-censored under-call rate (MIC analogue of a very major error; clinical devices must stay below about 1.5 percent). Human-clinical development diagnostics (job 64983779 outputs, development only): AMRFinderPlus models under-call right-censored rows 3.7 to 4.2 percent (ciprofloxacin), 10.8 to 16.8 percent (ceftriaxone), 14.0 to 18.7 percent (gentamicin), so no model is clinically usable; the no-genome constant scores 1.000 on left-censored and 0.000 on right-censored rows. Evo 2-only XGBoost failed on ciprofloxacin only in outer fold 1, which holds the SLV:ST131 group (EA 0.254 on 934 ST131 rows versus 0.902 for AMRFinderPlus XGBoost on the same rows; other folds 0.896 to 0.922): an embedding tree model fails when the dominant lineage is unseen; ridge on Evo 2 features did not (ST131 0.869). Pretraining overlap: OpenGenome2 (arcinstitute/opengenome2) uses one representative genome per GTDB species (releases 214.1 and 220; the species_metadata.csv of 28,177 species lists only the release-220 additions and contains no Escherichia) plus IMG/PR plasmids, IMG/VR phages and metagenomes; the E. coli representative GCF_003697165.2 is not among the 13,493 cohort genome requests. Plasmid audit job 64994989 submitted (IMG/PR blastn of every unique acquired unit). Evaluator reference-class reporting, ablation feature sets (amr+evo2_panel, amr+evo2_acquired) and the audit are implemented with tests; 391 local tests pass.

Pretraining-overlap audit job 64994989 COMPLETE (5m03s; results/genomics/pretraining-overlap/64994989/overlap.json with artifact hashes). Chromosomes: OpenGenome2 represents E. coli by the single GTDB species representative GCF_003697165.2, which is not among the cohort genomes. Plasmids: of 22,767 unique acquired units searched against the OpenGenome2 IMG/PR set Evo 2 was trained on, 14,482 (64 percent) have a near-identical copy (identity >= 99 percent over >= 95 percent of the unit), 5,013 a close copy (>= 90 over >= 80) and 3,272 none; over isolate-unit rows 75,279 near-identical, 25,392 close, 25,610 not found. Common mobile determinants are near-identical almost always (sul1 4,703 of 4,931 rows, sul2 5,202 of 5,460, tet(A) 5,196 of 5,355, dfrA17 2,755 of 2,832, mph(A) 3,119 of 3,171, blaTEM-1 3,362 of 5,075). Not-found rows are dominated by intrinsic chromosomal genes that AMRFinderPlus reports as Subtype AMR (acrF 12,948, emrD 9,010), which are near-universal and therefore mostly lineage markers inside the acquired-unit mean embedding; the ablation must be read with this in mind. Overlap cannot leak MIC labels (Evo 2 saw no phenotype); it establishes that most acquired determinants were in-distribution for the model.

Diagnosis of the human-clinical gentamicin Evo 2 gain (development only; ablation 65006996, ridge AMR versus AMR + acquired-unit Evo 2). The rare-variant hypothesis is rejected: all 23 resistant rows rescued by Evo 2 carry common determinants (aac(3)-IId 246 isolates, aac(3)-IIe 205; rare determinants occur in only 3 resistant isolates, none rescued). Net gain is +83 rows on exact references and +21 on right-censored, 0 on left-censored; among exact rows it is +89 for isolates with no gentamicin determinant (EA 0.325 to 0.546, references mostly 1 to 2 mg/L) and -6 for carriers. 106 of 109 fixed no-determinant exact rows and 22 of 23 fixed resistant rows come from one BioProject, PRJNA1297298 (University of Liverpool, 762 clinical isolates 'selected to provide a broad range of minimum inhibitory concentration phenotypes for machine learning'), which supplies 14.9 percent of human-clinical gentamicin rows. Excluding that project, EA is 0.965 for both models: the Evo 2 gentamicin gain is entirely source-specific. Interpretation: Evo 2 acquired-unit features let the model recognise isolates from one phenotype-enriched collection whose laboratory reports susceptible gentamicin MICs as exact 1 to 2 mg/L values, a source and measurement-convention signal rather than gentamicin biology; lineage-grouped CV does not prevent this because a source spans many lineages. The pre-registered credit rule stands (condition 1 was met; condition 2, the single-laboratory external evaluation, decides), and this diagnosis is reported with it.
